title: Kingship in Israel
lead: Israel was led for generations without a king. Deuteronomy allows a king but limits him: he must be an Israelite, must not pile up horses, wives or gold, and must copy and read the law (Deuteronomy 17:14–20). Samuel warns of what kings will take (1 Samuel 8), the books of Kings judge each ruler by the law, and the prophets look for a righteous king from David's line.
